governanceNotes: D1 batch 56 (2026-09-25): one bounded association edge authored - loss-of-tongue to dysphagia (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE. The proposition rests on glossectomy functional cohorts: the 30-patient deglutition series documents a progressive decline in swallowing with increasing extent of tongue loss (p = 0.001) (PMID 42152199), the 206-patient cohort documents speech-and-swallowing functional burden with tube-dependence tracking (PMID 42693646), and the prospective compartmental-glossectomy series documents delayed oral feeding with videofluoroscopic assessment (PMID 42218322).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-25: (i) excellent swallowing outcomes are documented after partial and most hemiglossectomies, so the burden is extent-dependent rather than universal; (ii) radiation and floor-of-mouth resection confound the oral-cancer cohorts; (iii) reconstruction recovers part of the function (all patients reached oral feeds within weeks under structured rehabilitation); (iv) age modifies recovery trajectory in the 206-patient cohort.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Glossectomy documents a graded swallowing burden: the 30-patient deglutition series found excellent swallowing in all partial glossectomies and 76 percent of hemiglossectomies but no excellent outcomes after near-total glossectomy, a progressive decline in swallowing with increasing extent of tongue loss (p = 0.001) (PMID 42152199), the 206-patient glossectomy cohort documents speech-and-swallowing functional concerns with gastrostomy-tube dependence tracked as an outcome (PMID 42693646), and the prospective compartmental-glossectomy series required delayed oral feeding at a mean of three weeks with swallowing assessed on videofluoroscopy (PMID 42218322); the co-occurrence is documented at dose-response and cohort class, so the edge records functional-risk only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the located material documents swallowing decline after tongue resection, but resection extent, floor-of-mouth involvement, reconstruction type, adjuvant radiation, and baseline function all require individual review before any causal statement.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Loss of tongue tissue abolishes the bolus manipulation, propulsion, and airway-protection mechanics of swallowing, producing dysphagia that scales with the extent of resection, the graded decline documented on validated swallowing measures, but whether any individual dysphagia arose from a given tongue loss remains hypothesized until videofluoroscopic and diet-level records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at dose-response and cohort class: the cohorts are oral-cancer-surgery populations where radiation and floor-of-mouth resection co-vary with tongue loss, reconstruction recovers part of the function, and excellent outcomes are documented after partial resection, so the magnitude depends on extent rather than the loss alone.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Excellent swallowing outcomes are documented after partial and most hemiglossectomies, so the burden is extent-dependent; radiation and floor-of-mouth resection confound the oral-cancer cohorts.

evidenceGaps: Excellent swallowing outcomes are documented after partial and most hemiglossectomies, so the burden is extent-dependent; radiation and floor-of-mouth resection confound the oral-cancer cohorts.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the anatomic-mechanics precedent, mirroring the ankyloglossia dysphagia window's bounded framing: the deglutition series of 30 tongue-reconstruction patients found a progressive decline in swallowing outcomes with increasing extent of glossectomy (p = 0.001) - excellent function in all partial and 76.19 percent of hemiglossectomies but none after near-total resection (PMID 42152199) - the 206-patient glossectomy cohort documents speech-and-swallowing functional outcomes with gastrostomy-tube and tracheostomy dependence tracked across age strata (PMID 42693646), and the prospective compartmental-glossectomy series documented all patients starting oral feeds at a mean of three weeks postoperatively with videofluoroscopic swallowing assessment (PMID 42218322); because the evidence is oral-cancer-surgery class where radiation and floor-of-mouth resection co-vary, reconstruction recovers part of the function, and partial resections reach excellent outcomes, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated videofluoroscopic swallowing studies with resection-extent documentation and competing-cause exclusion.
